hints.title: Grid Directed Transitions
hints.text: Moving strictly down or right ensures a topological order of cells without circular path dependencies.

hints.title: Alternating Direction Dimension
hints.text: Track two costs per cell based on whether the last movement step was horizontal or vertical.

hints.title: Goal State Combination
hints.text: The minimal total cost reaching the bottom-right corner is the minimum across both incoming directional states.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def minCost(self, grid: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        # dp[r][c][dir]: dir 0 is came vertically (can move horizontally), dir 1 is came horizontally (can move vertically)
        INF = float('inf')
        dp = [[[INF, INF] for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(m)]
        dp[0][0][0] = grid[0][0]
        dp[0][0][1] = grid[0][0]
        
        for r in range(m):
            for c in range(n):
                # Move right from (r, c - 1): arrives horizontally (dir 1), must have come vertically (dir 0)
                if c > 0 and dp[r][c - 1][0] != INF:
                    dp[r][c][1] = min(dp[r][c][1], dp[r][c - 1][0] + grid[r][c])
                # Move down from (r - 1, c): arrives vertically (dir 0), must have come horizontally (dir 1)
                if r > 0 and dp[r - 1][c][1] != INF:
                    dp[r][c][0] = min(dp[r][c][0], dp[r - 1][c][1] + grid[r][c])
                    
        ans = min(dp[m - 1][n - 1][0], dp[m - 1][n - 1][1])
        return ans if ans != INF else -1
```

complexity.notes: Two-state dynamic programming grid traversal in topological cell order.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive path enumeration without memoization explores exponential routes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: DP table of size M x N x 2 stores minimum costs per arrival direction.
